messages:
ashley: quick heads-up — ran the nightly matmul sweep for the long-seq batch (seq=8k, batch=4) and seen a big latency spike in a subset of traces. nsys shows cuBLASLt switching to an algo with >200MB workspace then long device-to-device memcpy stalls.

matt: can you paste the nsys cmd & a small timeline snippet?

ashley: ran `nsys profile --trace=cuda,nvtx --stats=true -o run_8k ./runner --config config/8k.json` and saved perfetto .qdrep. here's the NVTX region dump from the hot trace: `MatMul(lt_algo=8, workspace=218MB) -> GEMM_LT_KERNEL -> memcpy.D2D(200MB) -> wait_event`

jia: omg workspace 218MB? that's huge for sequence 8k with batch 4. what were input dtypes/quant?

ashley: float16, no quantization, model: 7B-ish, kv cache present. interestingly, the traces where algo=8 happened clustered when KV cache hit ratio was >0.9 in the same process. when KV cache cold, cuBLASLt chose algo 3 (tiny workspace).

leo: maybe the runtime heuristic is using combined problem size (seq*batch) and overestimating optimal algo because KV cache changes effective active seq length?

matt: that's plausible — if prefix caching yields longer effective matmul lengths for certain microbatches, the heuristic might pick higher-workspace algos. we should check the exact matmul dims passed to cublasLt for each NVTX region.

ashley: attached matmul dims from the trace: `[M=12288, N=12288, K=4096]` for the heavy windows. when algo=3 dims were `[M=1024, N=4096, K=4096]` — so there's a big change.

jia: wait those dims are way off expected. are you sure the KV cache merge is being sampled in the profiler? maybe our merged-kv path concatenates prefixes before the matmul op and the profiler is capturing the post-concat shape.

ashley: yep NVTX shows `pre-kv-concat` and `post-kv-concat` regions. post-kv-concat triggers the big GEMM. looks like some requests hit a cached prefix and we run an amortized bigger matmul for a few tokens then short ones after.

matt: timeline-level view would help — can we load perfetto and look for kernel overlap and queue depths? also get `cudaMemGetInfo` around the times to see fragmentation.

ashley: perfetto attached (link internal) — I pulled a heatmap: kernel occupancy dips during memcpy spikes and there are recurring small kernels queued behind big workspace allocs. `cudaMalloc`/`cudaFree` churn visible.

leo: that implies workspace allocation strategy is hurting — cuBLASLt algos that need big scratch should use pooled allocator or reuse preallocated slab. do we have per-device workspace pool enabled for the private/runtime config?

ashley: config shows `workspace_pool: enabled` but only for dedicated flows. this trace was on a shared-hosted node where we fallback to ephemeral `cudaMalloc` for each call.

jia: there we go. ephemeral mallocs + big workspace cause fragmentation and D2D memcpys while freeing previous large buffers. that can stall the stream and reorder kernels.

matt: two-pronged fix: 1) adjust algo selection heuristic to penalize workspace-heavy algos on shared nodes, 2) enable a fallback pooled allocator for hosted infra. also consider a fast-path to prefer cuBLASLt algo variants that avoid extra D2D copies when KV cache present.

ashley: agreed. i prototyped a quick heuristic: if `device_free_mem < 0.3 * algo_workspace`, prefer lower-workspace algos; on traces that reduces freq of algo=8 from ~18% -> 2% and removes the big memcpy windows.

leo: nice. can you add the heuristic and rerun the same sweep? also add an NVTX tag with the `algo_choice` and `workspace_bytes` so perf traces are clearer.

ashley: on it. i'll push a small CL to runtime algo selector and re-run nsys. also will dump `cublasLtGetAlgoInfo` for each chosen algo into logs.

matt: once you have the new traces, let’s run a perf regression check: compare p50/p95 latency and token throughput across the same seeds. if mean improves and p99 drops, feel comfortable rolling to canary.

jia: add a test that simulates high KV-hit microbatching (patterned requests that bounce between cold and warm prefixes). we need to ensure the heuristic doesn't regress isolated full-length workloads (e.g., dedicated cases where workspace is fine).

leo: also document the behavior in eng-runtime/notes — include a quick figure from perfetto showing timeline before/after. this will help infra to toggle pool on hosted if needed.

ashley: pushing traces now. small excerpt of runtime log for reference:
```[2026-02-28T14:02:11Z] nvtx: MatMul region start dims=M=12288,N=12288,K=4096
[2026-02-28T14:02:11Z] cublasLt: chosen_algo=8 workspace=228170624
[2026-02-28T14:02:12Z] cudaMalloc -> 228170624 bytes
[2026-02-28T14:02:12Z] memcpy.D2D 228170624 bytes duration=18ms
[2026-02-28T14:02:12Z] MatMul complete elapsed=54ms
```

matt: that memcpy is the culprit. 18ms D2D is huge relative to typical matmul times.

ashley: after heuristic CL, excerpt shows `chosen_algo=3 workspace=10485760` and no cudaMalloc for big slab. end-to-end p95 dropped 24%.

jia: great. please open an RFC for two things: a) heuristic in selector (with metrics), b) hosted pooled-workspace rollout plan. include safety toggles for dedicated vs hosted.

leo: +1. also add an infra flag to force `prefer_low_workspace=true` per host-class so we can toggle while we observe.

ashley: created PR #4821 for the selector and uploaded before/after traces to the incident artifacts bucket. i'll ping infra to discuss enabling pool in hosted.

infra-bot: deploy_bot: perf-sweep-v2 started on host group 'hosted-gpu-XX' — monitoring p50/p95 for next 30m.

matt: awesome — follow-up in ~1hr after the sweep finishes. thanks all, solid catch. :thumbsup:
